mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has stabilized at -21.9% over the last two weeks, indicating a floor in remote work adoption. This stability signals employers are not further reducing on-site presence, allowing retail-adjacent commuting patterns to resume incrementally, driving RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES at -21.9% in both t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days declines or remains flat relative to the prior 28-day mean, or WORKPLACES falls below -25% in any of the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has declined sharply from -16.9% to -31.1% over three weeks, then partially recovered to -23.4%, indicating weather-driven or policy-driven suppression of outdoor activity. As outdoor constraints ease, substitution behavior redirects foot traffic from parks to retail venues, increasing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 5 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS recovered 7.7 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS mobility does not improve by at least 3 percentage points in the first two weeks of the forecast period, or RETAIL_REC declines despite PARKS recovery.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has remained depressed at -32.9% to -37.7% across all four weeks, reflecting ongoing transit restrictions or low confidence. If transit capacity constraints are lifted, commuting accessibility improves, enabling retail foot traffic to rise. RETAIL_REC will increase if TRANSIT rises above -25% within the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT consistently below -32% across all four weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT remains below -30% for all four weeks of the forecast period, or RETAIL_REC does not increase despite TRANSIT crossing -25%.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has remained stable and only slightly negative (-4.3% to -7.4%), indicating essential shopping is resilient. This stability, combined with modest WORKPLACES recovery signals, suggests consumers are regaining confidence in public spaces. Joint stability in both series predicts RETAIL_REC will rise as discretionary spending confidence follows essential-goods normalization.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM variance is 3.1 points vs RETAIL_REC variance of 3.8 points
failure_condition: Either GROCERY_PHARM falls below -10% or WORKPLACES falls below -25% in any week of the forecast period, or RETAIL_REC does not rise relative to the prior 28-day baseline.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined from 12.7% to 10.9% over the last two weeks, indicating a marginal shift away from home-based activity. This outflow from residential spaces, if sustained, signals consumers are increasingly willing to venture to retail venues. The directional shift in RESIDENTIAL predicts RETAIL_REC will increase over the next four weeks as the trend continues.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 10% in any week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined 1.8 points from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL rebounds above 12% in any of the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not increase despite sustained RESIDENTIAL decline.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has shown high volatility (-16.9% to -31.1% to -23.4%), consistent with seasonal weather sensitivity in mid-March. If outdoor conditions improve, PARKS will recover sharply. Concurrent RETAIL_REC decline (-29.9% to -26.9%) suggests substitution: as PARKS recovers, retail will remain suppressed as consumers redirect to outdoor venues. RETAIL_REC will decline or stagnate over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS volatility of 15.1 points across four weeks
failure_condition: PARKS does not improve beyond -15%, or RETAIL_REC increases despite PARKS recovery above -15%.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are jointly suppressed, indicating coordinated restrictions on commuting infrastructure and workplace access. If both series remain below -30% and -22% respectively, retail venues will continue to experience suppressed foot traffic due to limited commuter throughput. RETAIL_REC will remain negative or decline further over the next four weeks under this regime.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT below -30 AND WORKPLACES below -22
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -32.9% and WORKPLACES at -21.9% in t-0w
failure_condition: Either TRANSIT rises above -25% or WORKPLACES rises above -15% in any week, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 percentage points relative to the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has shown a modest upward trend from -29.9% to -26.9% over four weeks, indicating gradual consumer confidence recovery. This trend is independent of external shocks and reflects intrinsic behavioral normalization. If this trend continues linearly, RETAIL_REC will rise further to approximately -24% over the next four weeks, driven by accumulated confidence effects.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 3.0 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines by more than 2 percentage points in any single week of the forecast period, or the 28-day mean does not exceed the prior 28-day mean.
